notes: My Cashbook has been rebuilt around your books. The screen now opens on a list of every book you keep — what each one has cost, when it was last touched, and who else is on it — with a search box and a sort, and an Add new book button at the bottom. Open a book and you get the ledger itself: search by remark or amount, filter by date, entry type, status, category or payment mode, a Net Balance card that recalculates as you filter, and your entries grouped day by day with a running balance and who added each one. Cash In and Cash Out sit permanently at the bottom of the book, so recording something takes a couple of taps. You can now share a book with a colleague. Invite anyone from your company, they accept, and from then on you both file into the same book — but what each of you spends still comes out of your own advance, never theirs, and the book simply adds it up. Give someone the view-only role instead and they can read the book and pull its reports without changing anything. Removing somebody later never touches the entries they already made. Money that comes back into a book — a supplier refund, a cancelled booking, materials returned — can now be recorded as Cash In against that book, with a bill, and it comes off what the book has cost. Reports have been rewritten: pick All entries, a Day-wise summary or a Category-wise summary, generate it as a PDF or a spreadsheet, and it covers exactly what you had filtered on screen. The word khata has been retired throughout — a khata is now simply a book, Employee Advances is Employee Cashbook, and the company cashbook is Company Accounts. For the accounts team, the Expenses to confirm queue had been showing nothing at all because of a fault in how it asked the server; it now lists every expense and refund waiting to be checked, and everyone who holds cashbook access is told when an advance is requested rather than only whoever happened to be next in line.
